instruction: Stage all modifications, make a commit labeled 'initial setup', and check from the command line that the commit author matches.

command: git config --global user.name "xlang" && git config --global user.email "xlang2024anonym@gmail.com" && mkdir -p /home/user/projects/remote_project && cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git init --initial-branch=main && git config receive.denyCurrentBranch ignore
unzip -q /home/user/Downloads/binder.zip -d /home/user/projects/ && cd /home/user/projects/binder && git init --initial-branch main && git remote add origin /home/user/projects/remote_project

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to add changes, commit with message 'initial setup', and verify author. Evaluator checks git log output contains both the commit message 'initial setup' and author name 'xlang'. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric and vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the commit message 'initial setup' is present in the most recent commit
Evaluator correctly verifies the author 'xlang' is present in the commit
Git command format '%s | %an' appropriately extracts both commit message and author name in a single output line
check_include_exclude metric correctly checks that both required strings ('initial setup' and 'xlang') are present in the output
Edge cases are handled appropriately (no commit returns None/empty, wrong message/author will fail the include check)
get_rule() correctly returns rules dict directly, and check_include_exclude uses rules.get('include') to access the list
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator doesn't explicitly verify that changes were staged/added before committing, only that a commit exists. However, this is acceptable because a successful commit creation implies the staging step succeeded (git doesn't allow commits without staged changes unless using --allow-empty flag)
